segments.tr: تتغير إصدارات البيانات وطرق الاستطلاع بمرور الوقت، لذا استشر الناشرين الأصليين للحصول على الأرقام والمنهجية الحالية.*

fr.title: Moral vs. Argent : Pourquoi les enquêtes sur le moral des consommateurs manquent souvent ce que les acheteurs font réellement

segments.src: Every month, headlines announce that Americans are feeling gloomy about the economy.
segments.tr: Chaque mois, les titres annoncent que les Américains sont moroses face à l'économie.

segments.src: Every month, store traffic, card transactions and retail sales reports often tell a calmer story.
segments.tr: Chaque mois, la fréquentation des magasins, les transactions par carte et les rapports sur les ventes au détail racontent souvent une histoire plus calme.

segments.src: The two can seem like they describe different countries.
segments.tr: Les deux peuvent donner l'impression de décrire des pays différents.

segments.src: They don't.
segments.tr: Ce n'est pas le cas.

segments.src: They measure different things, and understanding the gap can make you a better reader of economic news.
segments.tr: Ils mesurent des choses différentes, et comprendre l'écart peut faire de vous un meilleur lecteur de l'actualité économique.

segments.src: ## What a consumer sentiment survey actually measures
segments.tr: ## Ce qu'une enquête sur le moral des consommateurs mesure réellement

segments.src: The best-known gauge in the United States is the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers.
segments.tr: L'indicateur le plus connu aux États-Unis est l'enquête sur les consommateurs de l'Université du Michigan (Surveys of Consumers).

segments.src: A separate widely cited measure, the Consumer Confidence Index, comes from The Conference Board.
segments.tr: Une autre mesure largement citée, l'indice de confiance des consommateurs (Consumer Confidence Index), provient du Conference Board.

segments.src: Both are built from questionnaires sent to a sample of households.
segments.tr: Les deux sont élaborés à partir de questionnaires envoyés à un échantillon de ménages.

segments.src: The Michigan survey asks respondents a set of questions about:
segments.tr: L'enquête du Michigan pose aux répondants une série de questions sur :

segments.src: - their own household's current finances compared with a year ago
segments.tr: - les finances actuelles de leur propre ménage par rapport à l'année précédente

segments.src: - their expectations for their finances over the next year
segments.tr: - leurs attentes concernant leurs finances au cours de l'année à venir

segments.src: - the outlook for the national economy over the short term and the next five years
segments.tr: - les perspectives de l'économie nationale à court terme et pour les cinq prochaines années

segments.src: - whether it is a good time to buy big-ticket items such as cars or appliances
segments.tr: - si le moment est opportun pour acheter des biens coûteux tels que des voitures ou des appareils électroménagers

segments.src: Answers are converted into index scores.
segments.tr: Les réponses sont converties en scores d'indice.

segments.src: The survey also asks about expected inflation, which policymakers and analysts watch closely.
segments.tr: L'enquête interroge également sur l'inflation attendue, que les décideurs politiques et les analystes surveillent de près.

segments.src: The key point is that these are **opinions and expectations**, not records of purchases.
segments.tr: Le point clé est qu'il s'agit d'**opinions et d'attentes**, et non de relevés d'achats.

segments.src: ## How the surveys are built
segments.tr: ## Comment les enquêtes sont élaborées

segments.src: A few design features shape what the numbers can and cannot tell you:
segments.tr: Quelques caractéristiques de conception façonnent ce que les chiffres peuvent et ne peuvent pas vous dire :

segments.src: - **Sampling.** Pollsters contact a few hundred to a few thousand people and weight the results to match the broader population. Smaller samples carry a margin of error, so a small monthly move may be statistical noise rather than a real shift.
segments.tr: - **Échantillonnage.** Les sondeurs contactent de quelques centaines à quelques milliers de personnes et pondèrent les résultats pour correspondre à la population globale. Les échantillons plus petits comportent une marge d'erreur, de sorte qu'une faible variation mensuelle peut être un bruit statistique plutôt qu'un réel changement.

segments.src: - **Method changes.** Over the years, many surveys have moved from telephone interviews to online panels. Response rates have fallen across the polling industry, and a change in method can change results, making long-run comparisons harder.
segments.tr: - **Changements de méthode.** Au fil des ans, de nombreuses enquêtes sont passées d'entretiens téléphoniques à des panneaux en ligne. Les taux de réponse ont chuté dans l'ensemble du secteur des sondages, et un changement de méthode peut modifier les résultats, rendant les comparaisons à long terme plus difficiles.

segments.src: - **Question wording.** Questions that ask about "the economy" invite broad, emotional answers. Questions about personal finances tend to be more grounded.
segments.tr: - **Formulation des questions.** Les questions qui portent sur « l'économie » incitent à des réponses larges et émotionnelles. Les questions sur les finances personnelles ont tendance à être plus ancrées dans la réalité.

segments.src: - **Timing.** Surveys capture a snapshot over a few weeks. News events in that window can color responses.
segments.tr: - **Calendrier.** Les enquêtes capturent un instantané sur quelques semaines. Les événements d'actualité au cours de cette période peuvent influencer les réponses.

segments.src: None of this makes the surveys useless.
segments.tr: Rien de tout cela ne rend les enquêtes inutiles.

segments.src: It means they should be read as one input with known limits.
segments.tr: Cela signifie simplement qu'elles doivent être lues comme une donnée parmi d'autres, avec des limites connues.

segments.src: ## Why words and wallets can diverge
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi les paroles et les portefeuilles peuvent diverger

segments.src: Researchers have noted several reasons why what people say can differ from what they spend.
segments.tr: Les chercheurs ont relevé plusieurs raisons pour lesquelles ce que les gens disent peut différer de ce qu'ils dépensent.

segments.src: ### 1. Prices are felt more than they are counted
segments.tr: ### 1. Les prix se ressentent plus qu'ils ne se comptent

segments.src: Even when inflation slows, price *levels* remain higher than they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: Même lorsque l'inflation ralentit, les *niveaux* de prix restent plus élevés qu'il y a quelques années.

segments.src: Many households judge the economy by the cost of groceries, rent, insurance and gas.
segments.tr: De nombreux ménages jugent l'économie en fonction du coût des courses, du loyer, de l'assurance et de l'essence.

segments.src: A person can say conditions are poor because everyday items cost more, and still keep buying them, because they are necessities.
segments.tr: Une personne peut dire que la situation est mauvaise parce que les produits du quotidien coûtent plus cher, tout en continuant à les acheter parce qu'ils sont nécessaires.

segments.src: ### 2. Spending is concentrated among a subset of households
segments.tr: ### 2. Dépenses concentrées sur un sous-ensemble de ménages

segments.src: Total retail sales are dominated by higher-income households, which hold most of the wealth and account for a large share of discretionary spending.
segments.tr: Le total des ventes au détail est dominé par les ménages à revenus élevés, qui détiennent la majeure partie du patrimoine et représentent une grande part des dépenses discrétionnaires.

segments.src: If those households are comfortable thanks to rising stock portfolios or home values, aggregate spending can hold up even when lower-income households feel squeezed.
segments.tr: Si ces ménages sont à l'aise grâce à la hausse des portefeuilles boursiers ou de la valeur des logements, les dépenses globales peuvent se maintenir même si les ménages à faibles revenus se sentent sous pression.

segments.src: A survey of all households and a dollar-weighted spending total are weighting people differently.
segments.tr: Une enquête auprès de l'ensemble des ménages et un total de dépenses pondéré en dollars attribuent un poids différent aux individus.

segments.src: ### 3. Mood is influenced by news and politics
segments.tr: ### 3. Le moral est influencé par l'actualité et la politique

segments.src: Research has repeatedly found that sentiment readings can differ sharply depending on a respondent's political leanings and on the news they consume.
segments.tr: Des recherches ont montré à plusieurs reprises que les mesures du moral peuvent différer nettement en fonction des orientations politiques du répondant et des médias qu'il consomme.

segments.src: Partisan swings in sentiment can occur without any change in people's actual finances.
segments.tr: Des variations partisanes du moral peuvent se produire sans aucun changement dans les finances réelles des individus.

segments.src: That makes the headline number a mix of economic experience and broader attitudes.
segments.tr: Cela fait du chiffre principal un mélange d'expérience économique et d'attitudes plus générales.

segments.src: ### 4. People spend on habit and need
segments.tr: ### 4. Les gens dépensent par habitude et par besoin

segments.src: Daily life continues regardless of mood.
segments.tr: La vie quotidienne se poursuit quel que soit le moral.

segments.src: Rent is due, commutes happen, and children need shoes.
segments.tr: Le loyer doit être payé, les trajets quotidiens ont lieu et les enfants ont besoin de chaussures.

segments.src: Much consumer spending is routine, so it does not respond quickly to changes in outlook.
segments.tr: Une grande partie des dépenses de consommation est routinière, elle ne réagit donc pas rapidement aux changements de perspectives.

segments.src: ### 5. Credit and savings can bridge the gap
segments.tr: ### 5. Le crédit et l'épargne peuvent combler l'écart

segments.src: Households may feel pessimistic yet keep spending by drawing on savings, using credit cards, or using buy-now-pay-later plans.
segments.tr: Les ménages peuvent se sentir pessimistes tout en continuant à dépenser en puisant dans leur épargne, en utilisant des cartes de crédit ou en recourant à des options de paiement en plusieurs fois.

segments.src: That can sustain spending for a while, but it is not necessarily a sign of strength.
segments.tr: Cela peut soutenir les dépenses pendant un certain temps, mais ce n'est pas nécessairement un signe de solidité.

segments.src: Rising delinquencies or shrinking savings buffers can mean the pattern is harder to maintain.
segments.tr: L'augmentation des impayés ou la réduction des réserves d'épargne peuvent signifier que ce modèle est plus difficile à maintenir.

segments.src: ### 6. Pessimism can be a general habit
segments.tr: ### 6. Le pessimisme peut être une habitude générale

segments.src: Surveys also reflect a tendency to describe "the economy" more negatively than "my own situation."
segments.tr: Les enquêtes reflètent également une tendance à décrire « l'économie » de manière plus négative que « ma propre situation ».

segments.src: Many people report feeling fine personally while worrying about the country at large.
segments.tr: De nombreuses personnes déclarent se sentir bien personnellement tout en s'inquiétant pour le pays dans son ensemble.

segments.src: ## Where sentiment has been useful
segments.tr: ## Là où les données sur le moral se sont révélées utiles

segments.src: It would be wrong to dismiss sentiment data.
segments.tr: Il serait faux de rejeter les données sur le moral des consommateurs.

segments.src: It has value in specific ways:
segments.tr: Elles ont de la valeur de manières spécifiques :

segments.src: - **Inflation expectations.** What households expect can influence wage demands and pricing behavior, which is why central bankers monitor these questions.
segments.tr: - **Anticipations d'inflation.** Ce que les ménages prévoient peut influencer les revendications salariales et les comportements de fixation des prix, c'est pourquoi les banquiers centraux surveillent ces questions.

segments.src: - **Turning points.** Sharp, sustained deteriorations have at times appeared alongside slowdowns, particularly when job worries rise.
segments.tr: - **Points de retournement.** Des détériorations brutes et prolongées sont parfois apparues aux côtés de ralentissements économiques, en particulier lorsque les inquiétudes concernant l'emploi augmentent.

segments.src: - **Distribution of views.** Breakdowns by income, age or region can show who is under pressure, even if the total looks stable.
segments.tr: - **Répartition des opinions.** Les ventilations par revenu, âge ou région peuvent montrer qui est sous pression, même si le total semble stable.

segments.src: - **Big-ticket intentions.** Plans to buy homes, cars or appliances can offer early clues about interest-rate-sensitive sectors.
segments.tr: - **Intentions d'achats importants.** Les projets d'achat de logements, de voitures ou d'équipements électroménagers peuvent fournir des indices précoces sur les secteurs sensibles aux taux d'intérêt.

segments.src: ## What to compare it against: hard spending data
segments.tr: ## À quoi le comparer : les données réelles sur les dépenses

segments.src: To judge whether mood is translating into behavior, pair sentiment with measures of what people actually did:
segments.tr: Pour juger si le moral se traduit par des comportements réels, associez l'état d'esprit à des mesures de ce que les gens ont réellement fait :

segments.src: | Indicator | What it shows | Caveat |
segments.tr: | Indicateur | Ce qu'il montre | Mises en garde |

segments.src: | Census Bureau retail sales | Monthly sales at stores and online retailers | Reported in current dollars, so inflation can inflate the headline; revised often |
segments.tr: | Ventes au détail du Census Bureau | Ventes mensuelles dans les magasins et chez les commerçants en ligne | Rapportées en dollars courants, l'inflation peut donc gonfler le chiffre principal ; révisées souvent |

segments.src: | Personal consumption expenditures (BEA) | Broader spending including services | Released with a lag and revised |
segments.tr: | Dépenses de consommation personnelle (BEA) | Dépenses plus larges incluant les services | Publiées avec un décalage et révisées |

segments.src: | Real (inflation-adjusted) spending | Whether people are buying more goods, not just paying more | Depends on the price index used |
segments.tr: | Dépenses réelles (ajustées de l'inflation) | Si les gens achètent plus de biens, et pas seulement s'ils paient plus cher | Dépend de l'indice de prix utilisé |

segments.src: | Card and payment data from banks and processors | Near-real-time transaction patterns | Reflects each firm's customer base, not the whole country |
segments.tr: | Données de cartes et de paiements des banques et processeurs | Tendances des transactions en temps quasi réel | Reflète la clientèle de chaque entreprise, pas le pays entier |

segments.src: | Employment and wage data | The income that supports spending | Strong jobs can coexist with weak sentiment |
segments.tr: | Données sur l'emploi et les salaires | Les revenus qui soutiennent les dépenses | Un marché de l'emploi solide peut coexister avec un moral faible |

segments.src: | Savings rate and credit data | Whether spending is funded sustainably | Can change quickly |
segments.tr: | Taux d'épargne et données sur le crédit | Si les dépenses sont financées de manière durable | Peut changer rapidement |

segments.src: | Company earnings commentary | What retailers say about traffic and trade-down | Each firm's view is partial |
segments.tr: | Commentaires sur les résultats des entreprises | Ce que disent les détaillants sur la fréquentation et la montée du bas de gamme | La vision de chaque entreprise est partielle |

segments.src: ## A practical way to read the two together
segments.tr: ## Une méthode pratique pour lire les deux ensemble

segments.src: 1. **Look at trends, not single months.** A three-month average of sentiment and spending is far less noisy than one release.
segments.tr: 1. **Regardez les tendances, pas les mois isolés.** Une moyenne sur trois mois du moral et des dépenses comporte bien moins de bruit qu'une seule publication.

segments.src: 2. **Adjust for inflation.** Ask whether retail sales rose because people bought more or because prices rose.
segments.tr: 2. **Ajustez en fonction de l'inflation.** Demandez-vous si les ventes au détail ont augmenté parce que les gens ont acheté davantage ou parce que les prix ont augmenté.

segments.src: 3. **Check who is spending.** Look for splits between higher- and lower-income households and between goods and services.
segments.tr: 3. **Vérifiez qui dépense.** Cherchez les écarts entre les ménages à hauts et faibles revenus, ainsi qu'entre les biens et les services.

segments.src: 4. **Watch the financial plumbing.** Rising credit card balances and delinquencies alongside strong spending suggest a different story than spending funded by income growth.
segments.tr: 4. **Surveillez les engrenages financiers.** La hausse des soldes de cartes de crédit et des impayés parallèlement à des dépenses soutenues suggère une histoire différente de dépenses financées par la croissance des revenus.

segments.src: 5. **Compare expectations questions with current-conditions questions.** They often diverge, and the difference can be informative.
segments.tr: 5. **Comparez les questions sur les attentes avec les questions sur les conditions actuelles.** Elles divergent souvent, et cette différence peut être instructive.

segments.src: 6. **Treat surprises as questions, not conclusions.** A big gap between mood and spending is a prompt to investigate, not proof that either is wrong.
segments.tr: 6. **Traitez les surprises comme des questions, pas comme des conclusions.** Un grand écart entre le moral et les dépenses invite à enquêter, il ne prouve pas que l'un ou l'autre est faux.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## En conclusion

segments.src: Sentiment surveys capture how people feel and what they expect.
segments.tr: Les enquêtes sur le moral capturent ce que les gens ressentent et ce qu'ils prévoient.

segments.src: Spending data captures what they do.
segments.tr: Les données sur les dépenses capturent ce qu'ils font.

segments.src: Feelings and behavior often move together over long periods, but in the short run they can diverge for good reasons: prices are visible, spending is concentrated, opinions are colored by news, and routine purchases continue regardless of mood.
segments.tr: Les sentiments et le comportement évoluent souvent ensemble sur de longues périodes, mais à court terme, ils peuvent diverger pour de bonnes raisons : les prix sont visibles, les dépenses sont concentrées, les opinions sont teintées par l'actualité et les achats de routine se poursuivent quel que soit le moral.

segments.src: The most reliable approach is to avoid relying on any single number.
segments.tr: L'approche la plus fiable consiste à éviter de se fier à un seul chiffre.

segments.src: Use sentiment as a window into worries and expectations, use hard spending data as a record of behavior, and look for where the two agree or disagree.
segments.tr: Utilisez le moral comme une fenêtre sur les inquiétudes et les attentes, utilisez les données réelles sur les dépenses comme un registre du comportement, et recherchez les points de convergence ou de divergence.

segments.src: That gap is often where the most interesting part of the economic story lies.
segments.tr: C'est souvent dans cet écart que réside la partie la plus intéressante de l'histoire économique.

pt.title: Humor vs. Dinheiro: Por Que as Pesquisas de Confiança do Consumidor Muias Vezes Erram o Que os Consumidores Realmente Fazem

segments.src: Every month, headlines announce that Americans are feeling gloomy about the economy.
segments.tr: A cada mês, as manchetes anunciam que os americanos estão desanimados com a economia.

segments.src: Every month, store traffic, card transactions and retail sales reports often tell a calmer story.
segments.tr: A cada mês, o movimento nas lojas, as transações com cartão e os relatórios de vendas no varejo costumam contar uma história mais calma.

segments.src: The two can seem like they describe different countries.
segments.tr: Os dois podem parecer descrever países diferentes.

segments.src: They don't.
segments.tr: Eles não descrevem.

segments.src: They measure different things, and understanding the gap can make you a better reader of economic news.
segments.tr: Eles medem coisas diferentes, e entender a lacuna pode tornar você um leitor melhor de notícias econômicas.

segments.src: ## What a consumer sentiment survey actually measures
segments.tr: ## O que uma pesquisa de confiança do consumidor realmente mede

segments.src: The best-known gauge in the United States is the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers.
segments.tr: O indicador mais conhecido nos Estados Unidos é a Pesquisa de Consumidores da Universidade de Michigan.

segments.src: A separate widely cited measure, the Consumer Confidence Index, comes from The Conference Board.
segments.tr: Outra medida amplamente citada, o Índice de Confiança do Consumidor, vem do The Conference Board.

segments.src: Both are built from questionnaires sent to a sample of households.
segments.tr: Ambos são construídos a partir de questionários enviados a uma amostra de famílias.

segments.src: The Michigan survey asks respondents a set of questions about:
segments.tr: A pesquisa de Michigan faz aos entrevistados um conjunto de perguntas sobre:

segments.src: - their own household's current finances compared with a year ago
segments.tr: - as finanças atuais da sua própria família em comparação com um ano atrás

segments.src: - their expectations for their finances over the next year
segments.tr: - suas expectativas para suas finanças durante o próximo ano

segments.src: - the outlook for the national economy over the short term and the next five years
segments.tr: - as perspectivas para a economia nacional no curto prazo e nos próximos cinco anos

segments.src: - whether it is a good time to buy big-ticket items such as cars or appliances
segments.tr: - se é um bom momento para comprar itens de alto valor, como carros ou eletrodomésticos

segments.src: Answers are converted into index scores.
segments.tr: As respostas são convertidas em pontuações de índices.

segments.src: The survey also asks about expected inflation, which policymakers and analysts watch closely.
segments.tr: A pesquisa também pergunta sobre a inflação esperada, o que os formuladores de políticas e analistas acompanham de perto.

segments.src: The key point is that these are **opinions and expectations**, not records of purchases.
segments.tr: O ponto principal é que essas são **opiniões e expectativas**, não registros de compras.

segments.src: ## How the surveys are built
segments.tr: ## Como as pesquisas são construídas

segments.src: A few design features shape what the numbers can and cannot tell you:
segments.tr: Algumas características de design moldam o que os números podem e não podem lhe dizer:

segments.src: - **Sampling.** Pollsters contact a few hundred to a few thousand people and weight the results to match the broader population. Smaller samples carry a margin of error, so a small monthly move may be statistical noise rather than a real shift.
segments.tr: - **Amostragem.** Os institutos de pesquisa contatam de algumas centenas a alguns milhares de pessoas e ponderam os resultados para corresponder à população em geral. Amostras menores carregam uma margem de erro, portanto, uma pequena variação mensal pode ser ruído estatístico em vez de uma mudança real.

segments.src: - **Method changes.** Over the years, many surveys have moved from telephone interviews to online panels. Response rates have fallen across the polling industry, and a change in method can change results, making long-run comparisons harder.
segments.tr: - **Mudanças de método.** Ao longo dos anos, muitas pesquisas migraram de entrevistas por telefone para painéis online. As taxas de resposta caíram em toda a indústria de pesquisas, e uma mudança de método pode alterar os resultados, tornando as comparações de longo prazo mais difíceis.

segments.src: - **Question wording.** Questions that ask about "the economy" invite broad, emotional answers. Questions about personal finances tend to be more grounded.
segments.tr: - **Redação das perguntas.** Perguntas que questionam sobre "a economia" convidam a respostas amplas e emocionais. Perguntas sobre finanças pessoais tendem a ser mais fundamentadas na realidade.

segments.src: - **Timing.** Surveys capture a snapshot over a few weeks. News events in that window can color responses.
segments.tr: - **Timing.** As pesquisas capturam um retrato ao longo de algumas semanas. Eventos de notícias nessa janela podem influenciar as respostas.

segments.src: None of this makes the surveys useless.
segments.tr: Nada disso torna as pesquisas inúteis.

segments.src: It means they should be read as one input with known limits.
segments.tr: Significa apenas que elas devem ser lidas como um dado com limites conhecidos.

segments.src: ## Why words and wallets can diverge
segments.tr: ## Por que palavras e carteiras podem divergir

segments.src: Researchers have noted several reasons why what people say can differ from what they spend.
segments.tr: Pesquisadores notaram vários motivos pelos quais o que as pessoas dizem pode diferir do que elas gastam.

segments.src: ### 1. Prices are felt more than they are counted
segments.tr: ### 1. Os preços são mais sentidos do que calculados

segments.src: Even when inflation slows, price *levels* remain higher than they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: Mesmo quando a inflação desacelera, os *níveis* de preços permanecem mais altos do que há alguns anos.

segments.src: Many households judge the economy by the cost of groceries, rent, insurance and gas.
segments.tr: Muitas famílias julgam a economia pelo custo dos mantimentos, aluguel, seguro e combustível.

segments.src: A person can say conditions are poor because everyday items cost more, and still keep buying them, because they are necessities.
segments.tr: Uma pessoa pode dizer que as condições estão ruins porque os itens do dia a dia custam mais, e ainda assim continuar comprando-os, porque são necessidades.

segments.src: ### 2. Spending is concentrated among a subset of households
segments.tr: ### 2. Os gastos estão concentrados em um subgrupo de famílias

segments.src: Total retail sales are dominated by higher-income households, which hold most of the wealth and account for a large share of discretionary spending.
segments.tr: As vendas totais no varejo são dominadas por famílias de renda mais alta, que detêm a maior parte da riqueza e respondem por uma grande parcela dos gastos discricionários.

segments.src: If those households are comfortable thanks to rising stock portfolios or home values, aggregate spending can hold up even when lower-income households feel squeezed.
segments.tr: Se essas famílias estiverem confortáveis graças à valorização das carteiras de ações ou dos imóveis, os gastos agregados podem se manter firmes mesmo quando as famílias de menor renda se sentem pressionadas.

segments.src: A survey of all households and a dollar-weighted spending total are weighting people differently.
segments.tr: Uma pesquisa com todas as famílias e um total de gastos ponderado por dólares estão atribuindo pesos diferentes às pessoas.

segments.src: ### 3. Mood is influenced by news and politics
segments.tr: ### 3. O humor é influenciado por notícias e política

segments.src: Research has repeatedly found that sentiment readings can differ sharply depending on a respondent's political leanings and on the news they consume.
segments.tr: Pesquisas demonstraram repetidamente que as leituras de confiança podem diferir drasticamente dependendo das inclinações políticas do entrevistado e das notícias que ele consome.

segments.src: Partisan swings in sentiment can occur without any change in people's actual finances.
segments.tr: Oscilações partidárias no sentimento podem ocorrer sem qualquer mudança nas finanças reais das pessoas.

segments.src: That makes the headline number a mix of economic experience and broader attitudes.
segments.tr: Isso faz do número principal uma mistura de experiência econômica e atitudes mais amplas.

segments.src: ### 4. People spend on habit and need
segments.tr: ### 4. As pessoas gastam por hábito e necessidade

segments.src: Daily life continues regardless of mood.
segments.tr: A vida cotidiana continua, independentemente do humor.

segments.src: Rent is due, commutes happen, and children need shoes.
segments.tr: O aluguel vence, os deslocamentos acontecem e as crianças precisam de sapatos.

segments.src: Much consumer spending is routine, so it does not respond quickly to changes in outlook.
segments.tr: Boa parte dos gastos dos consumidores é rotineira, por isso não responde rapidamente a mudanças nas perspectivas.

segments.src: ### 5. Credit and savings can bridge the gap
segments.tr: ### 5. Crédito e poupança podem cobrir a lacuna

segments.src: Households may feel pessimistic yet keep spending by drawing on savings, using credit cards, or using buy-now-pay-later plans.
segments.tr: As famílias podem se sentir pessimistas, mas continuar gastando ao recorrer a poupanças, usar cartões de crédito ou utilizar modalidades de parcelamento como "compre agora, pague depois".

segments.src: That can sustain spending for a while, but it is not necessarily a sign of strength.
segments.tr: Isso pode sustentar os gastos por um tempo, mas não é necessariamente um sinal de força.

segments.src: Rising delinquencies or shrinking savings buffers can mean the pattern is harder to maintain.
segments.tr: O aumento da inadimplência ou a redução das reservas de poupança podem significar que o padrão é mais difícil de manter.

segments.src: ### 6. Pessimism can be a general habit
segments.tr: ### 6. O pessimismo pode ser um hábito geral

segments.src: Surveys also reflect a tendency to describe "the economy" more negatively than "my own situation."
segments.tr: As pesquisas também refletem uma tendência de descrever "a economia" de forma mais negativa do que "a minha própria situação".

segments.src: Many people report feeling fine personally while worrying about the country at large.
segments.tr: Muitas pessoas relatam estar bem pessoalmente, enquanto se preocupam com o país em geral.

segments.src: ## Where sentiment has been useful
segments.tr: ## Onde a confiança tem sido útil

segments.src: It would be wrong to dismiss sentiment data.
segments.tr: Seria um erro descartar os dados de confiança.

segments.src: It has value in specific ways:
segments.tr: Eles têm valor de maneiras específicas:

segments.src: - **Inflation expectations.** What households expect can influence wage demands and pricing behavior, which is why central bankers monitor these questions.
segments.tr: - **Expectativas de inflação.** O que as famílias esperam pode influenciar as reivindicações salariais e o comportamento de fixação de preços, razão pela qual os banqueiros centrais monitoram essas questões.

segments.src: - **Turning points.** Sharp, sustained deteriorations have at times appeared alongside slowdowns, particularly when job worries rise.
segments.tr: - **Pontos de virada.** Deteriorações acentuadas e sustentadas às vezes surgiram ao lado de desacelerações, particularmente quando as preocupações com o emprego aumentam.

segments.src: - **Distribution of views.** Breakdowns by income, age or region can show who is under pressure, even if the total looks stable.
segments.tr: - **Distribuição de opiniões.** Detalhamentos por renda, idade ou região podem mostrar quem está sob pressão, mesmo que o total pareça estável.

segments.src: - **Big-ticket intentions.** Plans to buy homes, cars or appliances can offer early clues about interest-rate-sensitive sectors.
segments.tr: - **Intenções de itens de alto valor.** Planos para comprar imóveis, carros ou eletrodomésticos podem oferecer pistas precoces sobre setores sensíveis às taxas de juros.

segments.src: ## What to compare it against: hard spending data
segments.tr: ## Com o que comparar: dados concretos de gastos

segments.src: To judge whether mood is translating into behavior, pair sentiment with measures of what people actually did:
segments.tr: Para julgar se o humor está se traduzindo em comportamento, combine o sentimento com medidas do que as pessoas realmente fizeram:

segments.src: | Indicator | What it shows | Caveat |
segments.tr: | Indicador | O que mostra | Ressalva |

segments.src: | Census Bureau retail sales | Monthly sales at stores and online retailers | Reported in current dollars, so inflation can inflate the headline; revised often |
segments.tr: | Vendas no varejo do Census Bureau | Vendas mensais em lojas físicas e varejistas online | Informado em dólares correntes, portanto a inflação pode inflar o número principal; revisado frequentemente |

segments.src: | Personal consumption expenditures (BEA) | Broader spending including services | Released with a lag and revised |
segments.tr: | Despesas de consumo pessoal (BEA) | Gastos mais amplos, incluindo serviços | Divulgado com atraso e revisado |

segments.src: | Real (inflation-adjusted) spending | Whether people are buying more goods, not just paying more | Depends on the price index used |
segments.tr: | Gastos reais (ajustados pela inflação) | Se as pessoas estão comprando mais mercadorias, não apenas pagando mais | Depende do índice de preços utilizado |

segments.src: | Card and payment data from banks and processors | Near-real-time transaction patterns | Reflects each firm's customer base, not the whole country |
segments.tr: | Dados de cartões e pagamentos de bancos e processadoras | Padrões de transações em tempo quase real | Reflete a base de clientes de cada empresa, não o país inteiro |

segments.src: | Employment and wage data | The income that supports spending | Strong jobs can coexist with weak sentiment |
segments.tr: | Dados de emprego e salários | A renda que sustenta os gastos | Empregos fortes podem coexistir com confiança fraca |

segments.src: | Savings rate and credit data | Whether spending is funded sustainably | Can change quickly |
segments.tr: | Taxa de poupança e dados de crédito | Se os gastos estão sendo financiados de forma sustentável | Pode mudar rapidamente |

segments.src: | Company earnings commentary | What retailers say about traffic and trade-down | Each firm's view is partial |
segments.tr: | Comentários de resultados das empresas | O que os varejistas dizem sobre movimento e migração para marcas mais baratas | A visão de cada empresa é parcial |

segments.src: ## A practical way to read the two together
segments.tr: ## Uma maneira prática de ler os dois juntos

segments.src: 1. **Look at trends, not single months.** A three-month average of sentiment and spending is far less noisy than one release.
segments.tr: 1. **Olhe para as tendências, não para meses isolados.** Uma média de três meses de sentimento e gastos é muito menos ruidosa do que uma única divulgação.

segments.src: 2. **Adjust for inflation.** Ask whether retail sales rose because people bought more or because prices rose.
segments.tr: 2. **Ajuste pela inflação.** Pergunte se as vendas no varejo subiram porque as pessoas compraram mais ou porque os preços subiram.

segments.src: 3. **Check who is spending.** Look for splits between higher- and lower-income households and between goods and services.
segments.tr: 3. **Verifique quem está gastando.** Procure por divisões entre famílias de renda mais alta e mais baixa e entre bens e serviços.

segments.src: 4. **Watch the financial plumbing.** Rising credit card balances and delinquencies alongside strong spending suggest a different story than spending funded by income growth.
segments.tr: 4. **Observe a estrutura financeira.** O aumento dos saldos de cartão de crédito e da inadimplência ao lado de gastos fortes sugere uma história diferente de gastos financiados pelo crescimento da renda.

segments.src: 5. **Compare expectations questions with current-conditions questions.** They often diverge, and the difference can be informative.
segments.tr: 5. **Compare as perguntas de expectativas com as perguntas de condições atuais.** Elas frequentemente divergem, e a diferença pode ser informativa.

segments.src: 6. **Treat surprises as questions, not conclusions.** A big gap between mood and spending is a prompt to investigate, not proof that either is wrong.
segments.tr: 6. **Trate as surpresas como perguntas, não como conclusões.** Uma grande lacuna entre o humor e os gastos é um convite para investigar, não uma prova de que um dos dois está errado.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## A conclusão

segments.src: Sentiment surveys capture how people feel and what they expect.
segments.tr: As pesquisas de confiança capturam como as pessoas se sentem e o que esperam.

segments.src: Spending data captures what they do.
segments.tr: Os dados de gastos capturam o que elas fazem.

segments.src: Feelings and behavior often move together over long periods, but in the short run they can diverge for good reasons: prices are visible, spending is concentrated, opinions are colored by news, and routine purchases continue regardless of mood.
segments.tr: Sentimentos e comportamentos costumam se mover juntos ao longo de grandes períodos, mas no curto prazo podem divergir por bons motivos: os preços são visíveis, os gastos são concentrados, as opiniões são influenciadas por notícias e as compras de rotina continuam independentemente do humor.

segments.src: The most reliable approach is to avoid relying on any single number.
segments.tr: A abordagem mais confiável é evitar depender de um único número.

segments.src: Use sentiment as a window into worries and expectations, use hard spending data as a record of behavior, and look for where the two agree or disagree.
segments.tr: Use a confiança como uma janela para preocupações e expectativas, use os dados concretos de gastos como um registro de comportamento e procure onde os dois concordam ou discordam.

segments.src: That gap is often where the most interesting part of the economic story lies.
segments.tr: Essa lacuna é frequentemente onde reside a parte mais interessante da história econômica.

in.title: Suasana Hati vs. Uang: Mengapa Survei Sentimen Konsumen Sering Kali Meleset dari Apa yang Sebenarnya Dilakukan Pembeli

segments.src: Every month, headlines announce that Americans are feeling gloomy about the economy.
segments.tr: Setiap bulan, tajuk berita mengumumkan bahwa warga Amerika merasa suram tentang perekonomian.

segments.src: Every month, store traffic, card transactions and retail sales reports often tell a calmer story.
segments.tr: Setiap bulan, lalu lintas toko, transaksi kartu, dan laporan penjualan ritel sering kali menunjukkan cerita yang lebih tenang.

segments.src: The two can seem like they describe different countries.
segments.tr: Keduanya seolah-olah menggambarkan negara yang berbeda.

segments.src: They don't.
segments.tr: Padahal tidak.

segments.src: They measure different things, and understanding the gap can make you a better reader of economic news.
segments.tr: Keduanya mengukur hal yang berbeda, dan memahami celah tersebut dapat membuat Anda menjadi pembaca berita ekonomi yang lebih baik.

segments.src: ## What a consumer sentiment survey actually measures
segments.tr: ## Apa yang sebenarnya diukur oleh survei sentimen konsumen

segments.src: The best-known gauge in the United States is the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers.
segments.tr: Tolok ukur paling terkenal di Amerika Serikat adalah Surveys of Consumers dari University of Michigan.

segments.src: A separate widely cited measure, the Consumer Confidence Index, comes from The Conference Board.
segments.tr: Ukuran lain yang juga banyak dikutip, Indeks Kepercayaan Konsumen (Consumer Confidence Index), berasal dari The Conference Board.

segments.src: Both are built from questionnaires sent to a sample of households.
segments.tr: Keduanya dibangun dari kuesioner yang dikirimkan ke sampel rumah tangga.

segments.src: The Michigan survey asks respondents a set of questions about:
segments.tr: Survei Michigan mengajukan serangkaian pertanyaan kepada responden tentang:

segments.src: - their own household's current finances compared with a year ago
segments.tr: - keuangan rumah tangga mereka saat ini dibandingkan dengan setahun yang lalu

segments.src: - their expectations for their finances over the next year
segments.tr: - ekspektasi mereka terhadap keuangan mereka selama tahun depan

segments.src: - the outlook for the national economy over the short term and the next five years
segments.tr: - prospek perekonomian nasional dalam jangka pendek dan lima tahun ke depan

segments.src: - whether it is a good time to buy big-ticket items such as cars or appliances
segments.tr: - apakah ini waktu yang baik untuk membeli barang-barang bernilai besar seperti mobil atau peralatan rumah tangga

segments.src: Answers are converted into index scores.
segments.tr: Jawaban diubah menjadi skor indeks.

segments.src: The survey also asks about expected inflation, which policymakers and analysts watch closely.
segments.tr: Survei ini juga menanyakan tentang ekspektasi inflasi, yang dipantau ketat oleh pembuat kebijakan dan analis.

segments.src: The key point is that these are **opinions and expectations**, not records of purchases.
segments.tr: Poin kuncinya adalah bahwa ini adalah **pendapat dan ekspektasi**, bukan catatan pembelian.

segments.src: ## How the surveys are built
segments.tr: ## Bagaimana survei dirancang

segments.src: A few design features shape what the numbers can and cannot tell you:
segments.tr: Beberapa fitur desain menentukan apa yang dapat dan tidak dapat disampaikan oleh angka-angka tersebut:

segments.src: - **Sampling.** Pollsters contact a few hundred to a few thousand people and weight the results to match the broader population. Smaller samples carry a margin of error, so a small monthly move may be statistical noise rather than a real shift.
segments.tr: - **Pengambilan sampel.** Penyelenggara jajak pendapat menghubungi beberapa ratus hingga beberapa ribu orang dan membobot hasilnya agar cocok dengan populasi yang lebih luas. Sampel yang lebih kecil membawa margin kesalahan, sehingga pergerakan bulanan yang kecil mungkin merupakan noise statistik alih-alih pergeseran nyata.

segments.src: - **Method changes.** Over the years, many surveys have moved from telephone interviews to online panels. Response rates have fallen across the polling industry, and a change in method can change results, making long-run comparisons harder.
segments.tr: - **Perubahan metode.** Selama bertahun-tahun, banyak survei beralih dari wawancara telepon ke panel daring. Tingkat respons telah menurun di seluruh industri jajak pendapat, dan perubahan metode dapat mengubah hasil, membuat perbandingan jangka panjang menjadi lebih sulit.

segments.src: - **Question wording.** Questions that ask about "the economy" invite broad, emotional answers. Questions about personal finances tend to be more grounded.
segments.tr: - **Pilihan kata pertanyaan.** Pertanyaan yang menanyakan tentang "perekonomian" memicu jawaban emosional yang luas. Pertanyaan tentang keuangan pribadi cenderung lebih realistis.

segments.src: - **Timing.** Surveys capture a snapshot over a few weeks. News events in that window can color responses.
segments.tr: - **Waktu.** Survei menangkap gambaran selama beberapa minggu. Peristiwa berita dalam rentang waktu tersebut dapat memengaruhi jawaban.

segments.src: None of this makes the surveys useless.
segments.tr: Tidak ada satu pun dari hal ini yang membuat survei menjadi tidak berguna.

segments.src: It means they should be read as one input with known limits.
segments.tr: Ini berarti survei harus dibaca sebagai salah satu masukan dengan batasan yang diketahui.

segments.src: ## Why words and wallets can diverge
segments.tr: ## Mengapa perkataan dan dompet bisa berbeda

segments.src: Researchers have noted several reasons why what people say can differ from what they spend.
segments.tr: Para peneliti telah mencatat beberapa alasan mengapa apa yang dikatakan orang bisa berbeda dari apa yang mereka belanjakan.

segments.src: ### 1. Prices are felt more than they are counted
segments.tr: ### 1. Harga lebih dirasakan daripada dihitung

segments.src: Even when inflation slows, price *levels* remain higher than they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: Bahkan ketika inflasi melambat, *tingkat* harga tetap lebih tinggi daripada beberapa tahun lalu.

segments.src: Many households judge the economy by the cost of groceries, rent, insurance and gas.
segments.tr: Banyak rumah tangga menilai perekonomian dari biaya bahan makanan, sewa, asuransi, dan bensin.

segments.src: A person can say conditions are poor because everyday items cost more, and still keep buying them, because they are necessities.
segments.tr: Seseorang dapat mengatakan kondisi buruk karena barang kebutuhan sehari-hari lebih mahal, namun tetap membelinya karena merupakan kebutuhan mendasar.

segments.src: ### 2. Spending is concentrated among a subset of households
segments.tr: ### 2. Pengeluaran terkonsentrasi pada sebagian rumah tangga

segments.src: Total retail sales are dominated by higher-income households, which hold most of the wealth and account for a large share of discretionary spending.
segments.tr: Total penjualan ritel didominasi oleh rumah tangga berpenghasilan lebih tinggi, yang memegang sebagian besar kekayaan dan menyumbang porsi besar dari pengeluaran diskresional.

segments.src: If those households are comfortable thanks to rising stock portfolios or home values, aggregate spending can hold up even when lower-income households feel squeezed.
segments.tr: Jika rumah tangga tersebut merasa nyaman karena portofolio saham atau nilai rumah yang naik, pengeluaran agregat dapat bertahan bahkan ketika rumah tangga berpenghasilan lebih rendah merasa tertekan.

segments.src: A survey of all households and a dollar-weighted spending total are weighting people differently.
segments.tr: Survei terhadap seluruh rumah tangga dan total pengeluaran terbobot dolar membobot orang secara berbeda.

segments.src: ### 3. Mood is influenced by news and politics
segments.tr: ### 3. Suasana hati dipengaruhi oleh berita dan politik

segments.src: Research has repeatedly found that sentiment readings can differ sharply depending on a respondent's political leanings and on the news they consume.
segments.tr: Penelitian berulang kali menemukan bahwa angka sentimen dapat sangat berbeda tergantung pada kecenderungan politik responden dan berita yang mereka konsumsi.

segments.src: Partisan swings in sentiment can occur without any change in people's actual finances.
segments.tr: Perubahan sentimen partisan dapat terjadi tanpa adanya perubahan pada keuangan nyata masyarakat.

segments.src: That makes the headline number a mix of economic experience and broader attitudes.
segments.tr: Hal itu membuat angka utama menjadi campuran antara pengalaman ekonomi dan sikap yang lebih luas.

segments.src: ### 4. People spend on habit and need
segments.tr: ### 4. Orang berbelanja berdasarkan kebiasaan dan kebutuhan

segments.src: Daily life continues regardless of mood.
segments.tr: Kehidupan sehari-hari terus berjalan terlepas dari suasana hati.

segments.src: Rent is due, commutes happen, and children need shoes.
segments.tr: Sewa harus dibayar, perjalanan kerja tetap terjadi, dan anak-anak membutuhkan sepatu.

segments.src: Much consumer spending is routine, so it does not respond quickly to changes in outlook.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar pengeluaran konsumen bersifat rutin, sehingga tidak merespons dengan cepat terhadap perubahan prospek.

segments.src: ### 5. Credit and savings can bridge the gap
segments.tr: ### 5. Kredit dan tabungan dapat menjembatani celah tersebut

segments.src: Households may feel pessimistic yet keep spending by drawing on savings, using credit cards, or using buy-now-pay-later plans.
segments.tr: Rumah tangga mungkin merasa pesimistis namun tetap berbelanja dengan menarik tabungan, menggunakan kartu kredit, atau menggunakan layanan beli sekarang bayar nanti (paylater).

segments.src: That can sustain spending for a while, but it is not necessarily a sign of strength.
segments.tr: Hal itu dapat mempertahankan pengeluaran untuk sementara waktu, namun belum tentu menjadi tanda kekuatan.

segments.src: Rising delinquencies or shrinking savings buffers can mean the pattern is harder to maintain.
segments.tr: Meningkatnya tunggakan atau menyusutnya penyangga tabungan dapat berarti pola tersebut semakin sulit dipertahankan.

segments.src: ### 6. Pessimism can be a general habit
segments.tr: ### 6. Pesimisme bisa menjadi kebiasaan umum

segments.src: Surveys also reflect a tendency to describe "the economy" more negatively than "my own situation."
segments.tr: Survei juga mencerminkan kecenderungan untuk menggambarkan "perekonomian" secara lebih negatif daripada "situasi saya sendiri."

segments.src: Many people report feeling fine personally while worrying about the country at large.
segments.tr: Banyak orang melaporkan merasa baik-baik saja secara pribadi sambil mengkhawatirkan negara secara keseluruhan.

segments.src: ## Where sentiment has been useful
segments.tr: ## Di mana sentimen terbukti berguna

segments.src: It would be wrong to dismiss sentiment data.
segments.tr: Menepis data sentimen begitu saja adalah hal yang keliru.

segments.src: It has value in specific ways:
segments.tr: Data ini memiliki nilai dalam cara-cara tertentu:

segments.src: - **Inflation expectations.** What households expect can influence wage demands and pricing behavior, which is why central bankers monitor these questions.
segments.tr: - **Ekspektasi inflasi.** Apa yang diharapkan rumah tangga dapat memengaruhi tuntutan upah dan perilaku penetapan harga, yang menjadi alasan mengapa bank sentral memantau pertanyaan-pertanyaan ini.

segments.src: - **Turning points.** Sharp, sustained deteriorations have at times appeared alongside slowdowns, particularly when job worries rise.
segments.tr: - **Titik balik.** Memburuknya sentimen secara tajam dan berkelanjutan terkadang muncul bersamaan dengan perlambatan ekonomi, terutama ketika kekhawatiran akan pekerjaan meningkat.

segments.src: - **Distribution of views.** Breakdowns by income, age or region can show who is under pressure, even if the total looks stable.
segments.tr: - **Distribusi pandangan.** Rincian berdasarkan pendapatan, usia, atau wilayah dapat menunjukkan siapa yang sedang dalam tekanan, meskipun totalnya terlihat stabil.

segments.src: - **Big-ticket intentions.** Plans to buy homes, cars or appliances can offer early clues about interest-rate-sensitive sectors.
segments.tr: - **Niat pembelian barang bernilai besar.** Rencana untuk membeli rumah, mobil, atau peralatan rumah tangga dapat memberikan petunjuk awal tentang sektor-sektor yang sensitif terhadap suku bunga.

segments.src: ## What to compare it against: hard spending data
segments.tr: ## Pembandingnya: data pengeluaran riil

segments.src: To judge whether mood is translating into behavior, pair sentiment with measures of what people actually did:
segments.tr: Untuk menilai apakah suasana hati terjemahkan ke dalam perilaku, sandingkan sentimen dengan ukuran dari apa yang sebenarnya dilakukan orang:

segments.src: | Indicator | What it shows | Caveat |
segments.tr: | Indikator | Apa yang ditunjukkan | Catatan |

segments.src: | Census Bureau retail sales | Monthly sales at stores and online retailers | Reported in current dollars, so inflation can inflate the headline; revised often |
segments.tr: | Penjualan ritel Census Bureau | Penjualan bulanan di toko dan pengecer daring | Dilaporkan dalam dolar saat ini, sehingga inflasi dapat membesarkan angka utama; sering direvisi |

segments.src: | Personal consumption expenditures (BEA) | Broader spending including services | Released with a lag and revised |
segments.tr: | Pengeluaran konsumsi pribadi (BEA) | Pengeluaran yang lebih luas termasuk jasa | Dirilis dengan tenggat waktu terlambat dan direvisi |

segments.src: | Real (inflation-adjusted) spending | Whether people are buying more goods, not just paying more | Depends on the price index used |
segments.tr: | Pengeluaran riil (disesuaikan inflasi) | Apakah orang membeli lebih banyak barang, bukan hanya membayar lebih mahal | Tergantung pada indeks harga yang digunakan |

segments.src: | Card and payment data from banks and processors | Near-real-time transaction patterns | Reflects each firm's customer base, not the whole country |
segments.tr: | Data kartu dan pembayaran dari bank serta pemroses | Pola transaksi mendekati waktu nyata (near-real-time) | Mencerminkan basis pelanggan masing-masing perusahaan, bukan seluruh negara |

segments.src: | Employment and wage data | The income that supports spending | Strong jobs can coexist with weak sentiment |
segments.tr: | Data lapangan kerja dan upah | Pendapatan yang mendukung pengeluaran | Lapangan kerja yang kuat dapat berdampingan dengan sentimen yang lemah |

segments.src: | Savings rate and credit data | Whether spending is funded sustainably | Can change quickly |
segments.tr: | Tingkat tabungan dan data kredit | Apakah pengeluaran didanai secara berkelanjutan | Dapat berubah dengan cepat |

segments.src: | Company earnings commentary | What retailers say about traffic and trade-down | Each firm's view is partial |
segments.tr: | Komentar pendapatan perusahaan | Apa yang dikatakan pengecer tentang lalu lintas toko dan penurunan kelas belanja (trade-down) | Pandangan masing-masing perusahaan bersifat parsial |

segments.src: ## A practical way to read the two together
segments.tr: ## Cara praktis untuk membaca keduanya secara bersamaan

segments.src: 1. **Look at trends, not single months.** A three-month average of sentiment and spending is far less noisy than one release.
segments.tr: 1. **Lihat tren, bukan bulan tunggal.** Rata-rata tiga bulan dari sentimen dan pengeluaran jauh lebih stabil dibanding satu kali rilis.

segments.src: 2. **Adjust for inflation.** Ask whether retail sales rose because people bought more or because prices rose.
segments.tr: 2. **Sesuaikan dengan inflasi.** Tanyakan apakah penjualan ritel meningkat karena orang membeli lebih banyak atau karena harga naik.

segments.src: 3. **Check who is spending.** Look for splits between higher- and lower-income households and between goods and services.
segments.tr: 3. **Periksa siapa yang berbelanja.** Cari perbedaan antara rumah tangga berpenghasilan lebih tinggi dan lebih rendah serta antara barang dan jasa.

segments.src: 4. **Watch the financial plumbing.** Rising credit card balances and delinquencies alongside strong spending suggest a different story than spending funded by income growth.
segments.tr: 4. **Amati sistem keuangan.** Meningkatnya saldo kartu kredit dan tunggakan bersamaan dengan pengeluaran yang kuat menunjukkan cerita yang berbeda dibandingkan pengeluaran yang didanai oleh pertumbuhan pendapatan.

segments.src: 5. **Compare expectations questions with current-conditions questions.** They often diverge, and the difference can be informative.
segments.tr: 5. **Bandingkan pertanyaan ekspektasi dengan pertanyaan kondisi saat ini.** Keduanya sering kali berbeda, dan perbedaan tersebut dapat memberikan informasi berharga.

segments.src: 6. **Treat surprises as questions, not conclusions.** A big gap between mood and spending is a prompt to investigate, not proof that either is wrong.
segments.tr: 6. **Perlakukan kejutan sebagai pertanyaan, bukan kesimpulan.** Celah besar antara suasana hati dan pengeluaran adalah dorongan untuk menyelidiki, bukan bukti bahwa salah satunya salah.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Kesimpulan

segments.src: Sentiment surveys capture how people feel and what they expect.
segments.tr: Survei sentimen menangkap bagaimana perasaan orang dan apa yang mereka harapkan.

segments.src: Spending data captures what they do.
segments.tr: Data pengeluaran menangkap apa yang mereka lakukan.

segments.src: Feelings and behavior often move together over long periods, but in the short run they can diverge for good reasons: prices are visible, spending is concentrated, opinions are colored by news, and routine purchases continue regardless of mood.
segments.tr: Perasaan dan perilaku sering kali bergerak bersama dalam jangka panjang, namun dalam jangka pendek keduanya dapat berbeda karena alasan yang jelas: harga terlihat nyata, pengeluaran terkonsentrasi, pendapat dipengaruhi oleh berita, dan pembelian rutin terus berlanjut tanpa memandang suasana hati.

segments.src: The most reliable approach is to avoid relying on any single number.
segments.tr: Pendekatan paling andal adalah menghindari ketergantungan pada satu angka saja.

segments.src: Use sentiment as a window into worries and expectations, use hard spending data as a record of behavior, and look for where the two agree or disagree.
segments.tr: Gunakan sentimen sebagai jendela untuk melihat kekhawatiran dan ekspektasi, gunakan data pengeluaran riil sebagai catatan perilaku, dan carilah di mana keduanya sejalan atau berseberangan.

segments.src: That gap is often where the most interesting part of the economic story lies.
segments.tr: Celah itulah yang sering kali menjadi bagian paling menarik dari cerita ekonomi.

segments.tr: *Artikel ini hanya untuk tujuan informasi umum dan bukan merupakan saran keuangan, investasi, atau ekonomi.

segments.tr: Rilis data dan metode survei berubah seiring waktu, jadi konsultasikan dengan penerbit asli untuk angka dan metodologi terkini.*

segments.src: ## How the surveys are built

segments.src: A few design features shape what the numbers can and cannot tell you:
segments.tr: いくつかの設計上の特徴が、数値が伝えられることと伝えられないことを形作っている：

segments.src: - **Sampling.** Pollsters contact a few hundred to a few thousand people and weight the results to match the broader population. Smaller samples carry a margin of error, so a small monthly move may be statistical noise rather than a real shift.
segments.tr: - **サンプリング。** 調査員は数百人から数千人に連絡を取り、結果をより広い人口に合わせてウェイト付けする。小さなサンプルには誤差の限界が伴うため、毎月の小さな変動は実際の変化ではなく統計的なノイズである可能性がある。

segments.src: - **Method changes.** Over the years, many surveys have moved from telephone interviews to online panels. Response rates have fallen across the polling industry, and a change in method can change results, making long-run comparisons harder.
segments.tr: - **手法の変更。** 長年にわたり、多くの調査は電話インタビューからオンラインパネルへと移行してきた。調査業界全体で回答率が低下しており、手法の変更が結果を変え、長期的な比較をより難しくしている。

segments.src: - **Question wording.** Questions that ask about "the economy" invite broad, emotional answers. Questions about personal finances tend to be more grounded.
segments.tr: - **質問の文言。** 「経済」について尋ねる質問は、広範囲で感情的な回答を招く。個人の家計に関する質問は、より現実的な傾向がある。

segments.src: - **Timing.** Surveys capture a snapshot over a few weeks. News events in that window can color responses.
segments.tr: - **タイミング。** 調査は数週間にわたるスナップショットを捉える。その期間内のニュースイベントが回答に色を付けることがある。

segments.src: None of this makes the surveys useless.
segments.tr: だからといって、調査が無意味になるわけではない。

segments.src: It means they should be read as one input with known limits.
segments.tr: それは、既知の限界を持つ一つのインプットとして読み解かれるべきであることを意味する。

segments.src: ## Why words and wallets can diverge
segments.tr: ## 言葉と財布が乖離する理由

segments.src: Researchers have noted several reasons why what people say can differ from what they spend.
segments.tr: 研究者らは、人々の言うことが消費する内容と異なる理由をいくつか指摘している。

segments.src: ### 1. Prices are felt more than they are counted
segments.tr: ### 1. 価格は数えられるよりも感じられることが多い

segments.src: Even when inflation slows, price *levels* remain higher than they were a few years ago.
segments.tr: インフレが鈍化しても、価格の*水準*は数年前よりも高いままである。

segments.src: Many households judge the economy by the cost of groceries, rent, insurance and gas.
segments.tr: 多くの世帯は、食料品、家賃、保険、ガソリンのコストによって経済を判断する。

segments.src: A person can say conditions are poor because everyday items cost more, and still keep buying them, because they are necessities.
segments.tr: 日常のアイテムの価格が高いため状況が悪いと言いながらも、それらが必需品であるため買い続けることはあり得る。

segments.src: ### 2. Spending is concentrated among a subset of households
segments.tr: ### 2. 消費は一部の世帯層に集中している

segments.src: Total retail sales are dominated by higher-income households, which hold most of the wealth and account for a large share of discretionary spending.
segments.tr: 全体の小売売上高は、富の大半を保有し裁量支出のかなりの割合を占める高所得世帯によって支配されている。

segments.src: If those households are comfortable thanks to rising stock portfolios or home values, aggregate spending can hold up even when lower-income households feel squeezed.
segments.tr: 株価の上昇や住宅価値のおかげでそうした世帯が快適であれば、低所得世帯が圧迫感を感じていても、総支出は持ちこたえることができる。

segments.src: A survey of all households and a dollar-weighted spending total are weighting people differently.
segments.tr: 全世帯の調査と、ドル換算の支出総額は、人々に異なるウェイトを置いている。

segments.src: ### 3. Mood is influenced by news and politics
segments.tr: ### 3. ムードはニュースや政治に影響される

segments.src: Research has repeatedly found that sentiment readings can differ sharply depending on a respondent's political leanings and on the news they consume.
segments.tr: 研究は、回答者の政治的傾向や消費するニュースによって、センチメントの数値が大きく異なる可能性があることを繰り返し発見している。

segments.src: Partisan swings in sentiment can occur without any change in people's actual finances.
segments.tr: センチメントにおける党派的な変動は、人々の実際の財政の変化なしに発生し得る。

segments.src: That makes the headline number a mix of economic experience and broader attitudes.
segments.tr: それが、ヘッドラインの数値を経済的経験とより広い態度の混合物にしている。

segments.src: ### 4. People spend on habit and need
segments.tr: ### 4. 人々は習慣や必要性に基づいて支出する

segments.src: Daily life continues regardless of mood.
segments.tr: 日々の生活はムードに関係なく続く。

segments.src: Rent is due, commutes happen, and children need shoes.
segments.tr: 家賃の支払いはあり、通勤があり、子どもには靴が必要である。

segments.src: Much consumer spending is routine, so it does not respond quickly to changes in outlook.
segments.tr: 多くの消費者支出はルーティンであるため、見通しの変化に対して素早く反応しない。

segments.src: ### 5. Credit and savings can bridge the gap
segments.tr: ### 5. クレジットと貯蓄がギャップを埋めることができる

segments.src: Households may feel pessimistic yet keep spending by drawing on savings, using credit cards, or using buy-now-pay-later plans.
segments.tr: 家計は悲観的を感じつつも、貯蓄を取り崩したり、クレジットカードを使用したり、今買っておき後で支払うプランを利用したりして支出を続けるかもしれない。

segments.src: That can sustain spending for a while, but it is not necessarily a sign of strength.
segments.tr: それはしばらく支出を維持できるが、必ずしも強さの兆候ではない。

segments.src: Rising delinquencies or shrinking savings buffers can mean the pattern is harder to maintain.
segments.tr: 延滞の増加や縮小する貯蓄バッファは、そのパターンを維持するのがより難しくなっていることを意味し得る。

segments.src: ### 6. Pessimism can be a general habit
segments.tr: ### 6. 悲観主義は一般的な習慣であり得る

segments.src: Surveys also reflect a tendency to describe "the economy" more negatively than "my own situation."
segments.tr: 調査はまた、「自分の状況」よりも「経済」をより否定的に描写する傾向を反映している。

segments.src: Many people report feeling fine personally while worrying about the country at large.
segments.tr: 多くの人々が、国全体を心配しながらも個人的には気分が良いと報告している。

segments.src: ## Where sentiment has been useful
segments.tr: ## センチメントが役立ってきた場所

segments.src: It would be wrong to dismiss sentiment data.
segments.tr: センチメントデータを退けるのは間違いである。

segments.src: It has value in specific ways:
segments.tr: それは特定の面で価値を持っている：

segments.src: - **Inflation expectations.** What households expect can influence wage demands and pricing behavior, which is why central bankers monitor these questions.
segments.tr: - **インフレ期待。** 家計が期待することは賃金要求や価格設定行動に影響を与える可能性があり、それが中央銀行がこれらの質問を監視する理由である。

segments.src: - **Turning points.** Sharp, sustained deteriorations have at times appeared alongside slowdowns, particularly when job worries rise.
segments.tr: - **転換点。** 急激で持続的な悪化は、特に雇用の心配が高まるときに、景気減速と並行して現れることがある。

segments.src: - **Distribution of views.** Breakdowns by income, age or region can show who is under pressure, even if the total looks stable.
segments.tr: - **見解の分布。** 所得、年齢、地域別の内訳は、全体が安定しているように見えても、誰がプレッシャーを受けているかを示すことができる。

segments.src: - **Big-ticket intentions.** Plans to buy homes, cars or appliances can offer early clues about interest-rate-sensitive sectors.
segments.tr: - **高額商品の意図。** 住宅、車、家電を購入する計画は、金利に敏感なセクターについての早期の手がかりを提供できる。

segments.src: ## What to compare it against: hard spending data
segments.tr: ## 比較すべき対象：ハードな支出データ

segments.src: To judge whether mood is translating into behavior, pair sentiment with measures of what people actually did:
segments.tr: ムードが行動に翻訳されているかどうかを判断するために、センチメントを人々が実際に行ったことの測定値とペアにする：

segments.src: | Indicator | What it shows | Caveat |
segments.tr: | 指標 | 示していること | 注意点 |

segments.src: | Census Bureau retail sales | Monthly sales at stores and online retailers | Reported in current dollars, so inflation can inflate the headline; revised often |
segments.tr: | 国勢調査局の小売売上高 | 店舗やオンライン小売業者での毎月の売上 | 現在のドルで報告されるため、インフレがヘッドラインを膨らませる可能性があり、頻繁に改定される |

segments.src: | Personal consumption expenditures (BEA) | Broader spending including services | Released with a lag and revised |
segments.tr: | 個人消費支出（BEA） | サービスを含むより広い支出 | ラグを伴って発表され、改定される |

segments.src: | Real (inflation-adjusted) spending | Whether people are buying more goods, not just paying more | Depends on the price index used |
segments.tr: | 実質（インフレ調整済み）支出 | 人々がより多くの財を買っているのか、単に多く支払っているだけなのか | 使用される価格指数に依存する |

segments.src: | Card and payment data from banks and processors | Near-real-time transaction patterns | Reflects each firm's customer base, not the whole country |
segments.tr: | 銀行やプロセッサーからのカードおよび決済データ | ほぼリアルタイムの取引パターン | 国全体ではなく、各企業の顧客ベースを反映している |

segments.src: | Employment and wage data | The income that supports spending | Strong jobs can coexist with weak sentiment |
segments.tr: | 雇用と賃金データ | 支出を支える収入 | 強い雇用は弱いセンチメントと共存し得る |

segments.src: | Savings rate and credit data | Whether spending is funded sustainably | Can change quickly |
segments.tr: | 貯蓄率とクレジットデータ | 支出が持続可能に資金提供されているかどうか | 急速に変化し得る |

segments.src: | Company earnings commentary | What retailers say about traffic and trade-down | Each firm's view is partial |
segments.tr: | 企業の収益コメント | 小売業者が客足やトレードダウンについて語ること | 各企業の見解は部分的である |

segments.src: ## A practical way to read the two together
segments.tr: ## 両者を一緒に読み解く実践的な方法

segments.src: 1. **Look at trends, not single months.** A three-month average of sentiment and spending is far less noisy than one release.
segments.tr: 1. **単月ではなくトレンドを見る。** センチメントと支出の3ヶ月平均は、1回の発表よりもはるかにノイズが少ない。

segments.src: 2. **Adjust for inflation.** Ask whether retail sales rose because people bought more or because prices rose.
segments.tr: 2. **インフレ調整をする。** 人々がより多く買ったために小売売上高が増加したのか、価格が上昇したためなのかを問う。

segments.src: 3. **Check who is spending.** Look for splits between higher- and lower-income households and between goods and services.
segments.tr: 3. **誰が支出しているかを確認する。** 高所得世帯と低所得世帯の間、および財とサービスの間の分裂を探す。

segments.src: 4. **Watch the financial plumbing.** Rising credit card balances and delinquencies alongside strong spending suggest a different story than spending funded by income growth.
segments.tr: 4. **金融の配管を監視する。** 強い支出と並行したクレジットカード残高の増加や延滞は、所得成長によって資金提供された支出とは異なるストーリーを示唆している。

segments.src: 5. **Compare expectations questions with current-conditions questions.** They often diverge, and the difference can be informative.
segments.tr: 5. **期待に関する質問を現在の状況に関する質問と比較する。** それらはしばしば乖離し、その違いは有益であり得る。

segments.src: 6. **Treat surprises as questions, not conclusions.** A big gap between mood and spending is a prompt to investigate, not proof that either is wrong.
segments.tr: 6. **サプライズを結論ではなく質問として扱う。** ムードと支出の間の大きなギャップは、どちらかが間違っているという証明ではなく、調査するための促しである。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## ボトムライン

segments.src: Sentiment surveys capture how people feel and what they expect.
segments.tr: センチメント調査は、人々がどのように感じ、何を期待しているかを捉える。

segments.src: Spending data captures what they do.
segments.tr: 支出データは、彼らが何をするかを捉える。

segments.src: Feelings and behavior often move together over long periods, but in the short run they can diverge for good reasons: prices are visible, spending is concentrated, opinions are colored by news, and routine purchases continue regardless of mood.
segments.tr: 感情と行動は長期間にわたって一緒に動くことが多いが、短期では正当な理由で乖離することがある：価格が見えること、支出が集中していること、意見がニュースによって色付けられていること、そして日常の購入がムードに関係なく続くことである。

segments.src: The most reliable approach is to avoid relying on any single number.
segments.tr: 最も信頼できるアプローチは、単一の数値に頼ることを避けることである。

segments.src: Use sentiment as a window into worries and expectations, use hard spending data as a record of behavior, and look for where the two agree or disagree.
segments.tr: 心配や期待への窓としてセンチメントを使用し、行動の記録としてハードな支出データを使用し、両者が一致または不一致している場所を探す。

segments.src: That gap is often where the most interesting part of the economic story lies.
segments.tr: そのギャップこそが、経済ストーリーの最も興味深い部分が潜んでいる場所であることが多い。

segments.src: *This article is for general informational purposes only and is not financial, investment or economic advice.
segments.tr: *この記事は一般的な情報提供のみを目的としており、財務、投資、または経済的なアドバイスではない。

segments.src: Data releases and survey methods change over time, so consult the original publishers for current figures and methodology.*
segments.tr: データ発表や調査方法は時間の経過とともに変化するため、現在の数値や方法論については元の発行元に相談のこと。*

de.title: Stimmung vs. Geld: Warum Verbraucherstimmungsindizes oft verfehlen, was Käufer tatsächlich tun

segments.src: Every month, headlines announce that Americans are feeling gloomy about the economy.
segments.tr: Jeden Monat verkünden Schlagzeilen, dass sich die Amerikaner pessimistisch hinsichtlich der Wirtschaft fühlen.

segments.src: Every month, store traffic, card transactions and retail sales reports often tell a calmer story.
segments.tr: Jeden Monat erzählen Ladenfrequenz, Kartentransaktionen und Einzelhandelsberichte oft eine ruhigere Geschichte.

segments.src: The two can seem like they describe different countries.
segments.tr: Die beiden scheinen unterschiedliche Länder zu beschreiben.

segments.src: They don't.
segments.tr: Das tun sie nicht.

segments.src: They measure different things, and understanding the gap can make you a better reader of economic news.
segments.tr: Sie messen unterschiedliche Dinge, und das Verständnis der Lücke kann Sie zu einem besseren Leser von Wirtschaftsnachrichten machen.

segments.src: ## What a consumer sentiment survey actually measures
segments.tr: ## Was eine Verbraucherstimmungsbefragung tatsächlich misst

segments.src: The best-known gauge in the United States is the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers.
segments.tr: Der bekannteste Indikator in den Vereinigten Staaten sind die Surveys of Consumers der University of Michigan.

segments.src: A separate widely cited measure, the Consumer Confidence Index, comes from The Conference Board.
segments.tr: Ein weiteres weit verbreitetes Maß, der Consumer Confidence Index, stammt vom The Conference Board.

segments.src: Both are built from questionnaires sent to a sample of households.
segments.tr: Beide basieren auf Fragebögen, die an eine Stichprobe von Haushalten gesendet werden.

segments.src: The Michigan survey asks respondents a set of questions about:
segments.tr: Die Michigan-Umfrage stellt Befragten eine Reihe von Fragen zu:

segments.src: - their own household's current finances compared with a year ago
segments.tr: - den aktuellen Finanzen des eigenen Haushalts im Vergleich zum Vorjahr

segments.src: - their expectations for their finances over the next year
segments.tr: - ihren Erwartungen an ihre Finanzen für das nächste Jahr

segments.src: - the outlook for the national economy over the short term and the next five years
segments.tr: - den Aussichten für die nationale Wirtschaft kurzfristig und in den nächsten fünf Jahren

segments.src: - whether it is a good time to buy big-ticket items such as cars or appliances
segments.tr: - ob es ein guter Zeitpunkt ist, langlebige Güter wie Autos oder Haushaltsgeräte zu kaufen

segments.src: Answers are converted into index scores.
segments.tr: Antworten werden in Indexwerte umgewandelt.

segments.src: The survey also asks about expected inflation, which policymakers and analysts watch closely.
segments.tr: Die Umfrage fragt auch nach der erwarteten Inflation, die politische Entscheidungsträger und Analysten genau beobachten.

segments.src: The key point is that these are **opinions and expectations**, not records of purchases.
segments.tr: Der Kernpunkt ist, dass dies **Meinungen und Erwartungen** sind, keine Kaufaufzeichnungen.

segments.src: ## How the surveys are built
segments.tr: ## Wie die Umfragen aufgebaut sind

segments.src: A few design features shape what the numbers can and cannot tell you:
segments.tr: Ein paar Designmerkmale prägen, was die Zahlen aussagen können und was nicht:

segments.src: - **Sampling.** Pollsters contact a few hundred to a few thousand people and weight the results to match the broader population. Smaller samples carry a margin of error, so a small monthly move may be statistical noise rather than a real shift.
segments.tr: - **Stichprobenziehung.** Meinungsforscher kontaktieren einige Hundert bis einige Tausend Personen und gewichten die Ergebnisse entsprechend der breiteren Bevölkerung. Kleinere Stichproben weisen eine Fehlerquote auf, sodass eine kleine monatliche Bewegung eher statistisches Rauschen als eine echte Verschiebung sein kann.

segments.src: - **Method changes.** Over the years, many surveys have moved from telephone interviews to online panels. Response rates have fallen across the polling industry, and a change in method can change results, making long-run comparisons harder.
segments.tr: - **Methodenänderungen.** Im Laufe der Jahre sind viele Umfragen von Telefoninterviews zu Online-Panels übergegangen. Die Rücklaufquoten sind in der gesamten Umfragebranche gesunken, und eine Änderung der Methode kann die Ergebnisse verändern, was langfristige Vergleiche erschwert.

segments.src: - **Question wording.** Questions that ask about "the economy" invite broad, emotional answers. Questions about personal finances tend to be more grounded.
segments.tr: - **Frageformulierung.** Fragen nach „der Wirtschaft“ laden zu breiten, emotionalen Antworten ein. Fragen zu persönlichen Finanzen neigen dazu, fundierter zu sein.

segments.src: - **Timing.** Surveys capture a snapshot over a few weeks. News events in that window can color responses.
segments.tr: - **Zeitpunkt.** Umfragen erfassen eine Momentaufnahme über einige Wochen. Nachrichteneignisse in diesem Zeitfenster können die Antworten färben.

segments.src: None of this makes the surveys useless.
segments.tr: Nichts davon macht die Umfragen nutzlos.

segments.src: It means they should be read as one input with known limits.
segments.tr: Es bedeutet, dass sie als ein Input mit bekannten Grenzen gelesen werden sollten.

segments.tr: ## Warum Worte und Geldbeutel auseinandergehen können
